transcript:
Header: Palmetto Retainer extension & Japan edge pilot check-in
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 09:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Sofia Morales (AE), Ethan Chu (SE), Riya Patel (CSM) -- Palmetto: Mina Tanaka (Head of ML), Kenji Saito (SRE), Lara Chen (Procurement), Hiro Ono (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, might be rough):
- Customer interested in extending retainer for another 12 months and adding Japan edge pilot (onprem-like VPC in ap-northeast region).
- Main concerns: latency to Japan (95th p95 goal ~80-100ms), cost delta for dedicated Japan nodes, data residency, and procurement timeline.
- Next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, SOC2 & KMS docs, pilot kickoff.

Topics: Retainer terms, Japan edge pilot scope, perf targets and test plan, security/compliance (KMS, SSO), procurement timeline.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Morales: hey everyone, um thanks for joining, i'm sofia from redwood, i'll run the agenda quick. we want to confirm extension details and scope the japan edge pilot, hope that works.
[00:12] Mina Tanaka: yes thanks, mina here. quick context — our product traffic to ap-northeast is ramping, latency to hosted endpoints is spiking during peak windows. we're evaluating a short pilot to put inference closer to our customers in japan.
[00:26] Ethan Chu: right, so from a tech pov we can do either a Dedicated pool in tokyo region or a Private VPC deployment. both have tradeoffs: dedicated gives predictable throughput on our managed infra; private gives more network isolation.
[00:40] Kenji Saito: to be clear, network e2e latency is the main metric — we want p95 generation latency under 100ms for our 1k token prompt workload. cost tolerance is limited; procurement wants to see unit economics.
[00:55] Riya Patel: procurement note captured. Lara, do you want to share your PO timeline?
[01:02] Lara Chen: yeah procurement — we run quarter-of-cycle purchasing; if we can get contract terms in by end of march we'd aim to sign in april. need net30 and standard security addendum. also need SOC2 docs and encryption details.
[01:15] Sofia Morales: understood. we can ship the SOC2 pack and KMS integration doc after the call. quick question — would you prefer a dedicated reserved pool in ap-northeast or a private VPC?
[01:27] Hiro Ono: from security perspective, private VPC with customer-managed peering is preferable; but it's heavier operationally. if dedicated can meet residency and logging requirements maybe that's acceptable.
[01:39] Mina Tanaka: also, we care about model variant compatibility — we run an Llama-derived model quantized to int8; need compatibility and kernel/quantization guidance. can redwood support that stack?
[01:54] Ethan Chu: yes, we onboard quantized variants and have kernel selection per arch; int8 is supported but we'll recommend a verification run. small note: sometimes transcription and model name formatting gets messy in our docs — apologies if i say things odd.
[02:09] Kenji Saito: (laughs) no worries. for the pilot we want to run realistic traffic: 500 rps sustained with 2k token sequences during peaks. is that feasible on a single dedicated node set?
[02:22] Ethan Chu: that depends on model size and batching. rule of thumb: for a 7B-class model with int8 on an A100-ish profile, 500 rps is high — we'd plan a 3-node pool with autoscaling/burst to handle spiky. we can propose exact sizing after the benchmark.
[02:40] Mina Tanaka: can we get a cost estimate ballpark now? rough is okay.
[02:45] Sofia Morales: rough math — dedicated reserved capacity with 3 nodes plus burst buffer would be roughly $Xk/month, pilot reduced term pricing we can layer in; i'll follow up with exact numbers.
[02:58] Lara Chen: Xk is plausible but please provide per-token and per-hour breakdown — procurement needs the unit economics line items.
[03:07] Sofia Morales: absolutely, will include per-token estimate, node-hour, egress.
[03:12] Kenji Saito: aside from latency, we need audit logs and key management. can you confirm KMS/HSM integration options and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM?
[03:24] Ethan Chu: yes — we support customer KMS for key wrapping and can forward audit logs over a secure endpoint or push to your S3 with lifecycle policies; we'll send the detailed ops playbook. tiny caveat: log retention beyond our default may be an add-on.
[03:40] Mina Tanaka: good. also about fallbacks — if japan region saturated will requests route to nearest region? that could spike latency which is not acceptable for some flows. we need predictable fallbacks.
[03:53] Riya Patel: product notes — we can set routing policies to prefer Japan and failover to Tokyo-dedicated backup only for non-critical flows. can document per-route SLOs.
[04:06] Hiro Ono: what's the SLA for dedicated Japan nodes?
[04:10] Sofia Morales: SLA is 99.9 for Dedicated with standard incident response; private deployments have different SLA because of customer infra. we can include SLA in amendment.
[04:20] Lara Chen: legal will need a data processing addendum for residency, can you send template?
[04:24] Sofia Morales: yes, sending DPA + standard security pack.
[04:27] Mina Tanaka: technical detail — for kv cache warmup, do you support prefix caching across nodes? we have many repeated prompts and want to avoid cold-start token penalties.
[04:40] Ethan Chu: yes we support prefix/KV caching and pre-warming strategies; for multi-node dedicated pools we replicate frequently used cache entries, and our routing tries to stick to warm nodes where possible. note: exact cache hit rates depend on your request distribution.
[04:55] Kenji Saito: perfect. one more: SSO and access control — need SAML SSO + RBAC for team members.
[05:02] Sofia Morales: supported — SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles, and token scoping available in console.
[05:10] Lara Chen: ok procurement aside, timeline reminders: we need pricing and contract by 3/25 to hit our internal sign window.
[05:18] Sofia Morales: we'll aim for that. Ethan, any notes on the benchmark plan?
[05:22] Ethan Chu: plan: 1) define test vectors with Mina 2) spin up a small dedicated pool in ap-northeast for 72 hours 3) run throughput + p95 runs across sampled prompts, include cold-start bursts and steady-state 4) collect token-level latencies and KV cache hit stats 5) deliver a short readout with recommended node sizing and expected per-token cost.
[05:46] Mina Tanaka: sounds good. timeline for the test infra?
[05:50] Ethan Chu: we can provision pilot infra within 5 business days after PO/contract signature; pilot itself 72 hrs over a week.
[05:57] Kenji Saito: can we get a trial credit/waived node-hour for the pilot?
[06:02] Sofia Morales: for committed customers extending retainer we can provide pilot credits; i'll propose an offset in the contract amendment.
[06:11] Lara Chen: helpful.
[06:13] Riya Patel: circling back to compliance — i'll attach SOC2 docs and answer questions; Sofia will send KMS and DPA.
[06:21] Sofia Morales: yes. any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:24] Hiro Ono: just two: exact per-token cost and network peering contact info.
[06:28] Sofia Morales: noted. Kenji will share peering contact and we'll propose cost breakdown.
[06:33] Mina Tanaka: one last thing, competitor checks — we've talked to LocalOps about a full onprem option; they claim lower latency but at higher ops cost. that tradeoff is still in evaluation.
[06:47] Sofia Morales: understood. our differentiator is unified ops and rollout controls plus built-in caching and reroute policies.
[06:55] Lara Chen: ok thanks. let's recap next steps now.
